reason: Judging throughput, not money, is now the binding constraint. The local judge runs at 1.1 rows/s (Qwen3-14B NF4) to 2.3 rows/s (Qwen3-8B bf16) on the NVIDIA L4 this run was migrated to, against about 23,000 unjudged rows. Batch size does not help: the L4 is power-capped at 72 W and the pass is prefill-bound.
changes: Local judge of record = Qwen/Qwen3-8B, bf16, prefill-only label scoring, byte-identical frozen v2 prompt. It matched the blind adjudication at least as well as Qwen3-14B-NF4 (kappa_R 0.59 vs 0.49) and pooled DEV agreement with gpt-4.1 is the same (0.60), so the faster model costs nothing measurable in agreement and roughly doubles how much of the design can be judged.
Qwen3-14B-NF4 labels are kept and used as a SECOND local reader, giving a per-cell reliability check on the cells where gemini labels do not exist (gemini only covers tier A and part of tier B).

TARGETED JUDGING QUEUE (src/local_judge.py JOB_PLAN), fixed here before the rows were judged, on the D300 item set so every cell shares the same items: (1) k0/P5/N5 in SL-MT and EN-BT = the primary contrast, the neutral specificity control and the conditioning set; (2) k0/P5 in EN-orig = the MT-noise arm; (3) P10/Pfull = the depth curve; (4) X5 = the cross-language 2x2; (5) P3/P20 = the rest of the curve. Anything not reached is reported as unjudged, never as null.

Consequences: the primary judged contrast is computed on D300 (300 items) rather than DEPTH-600, so its CI is about sqrt(2) wider; tier-D templates, the causal restoration grid and the collateral grid are NOT judged and are reported as unjudged with their label-free readouts only (steering vector norms, first-token KL, harmless NLL change, lexicon diagnostic). The causal claim is therefore NOT established in this artifact.
DEPTH-600 rows outside D300 keep their gemini labels in the ledger; they are not mixed into any local-judge statistic.
